title: Missing dates, the Chicago all-star band and New York bicycle races
summary: Looking for dates in his scrapbook, DeDroit tells of an all-star benefit band in Chicago and of playing the six-day bicycle races in New York, which led to offers from agents and Vincent Lopez, before he came home.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I left a look in this scrapbook. It's in here.
Well when did you make your records? Was it near the time you made your records? Yes. Well I can look that up you see.
I was making the records in those days.
Well we have books that tell all about your records.

You see if I had been like, I was doing so well and I was so busy that I didn't have time to put dates on anything or who the person was. I played in the All-Star Orchestra in Chicago when I was at the Green Mill. I played at the Green Mill in Chicago for Tom Chimali. And I was this trumpet player selected to play with all the stars and I can't tell you who they were and I know they must be all famous musicians. I went there to some big ballroom, we sat down, they handed out the music, we played it. The piano player gave us all a check and right now I don't remember one musician. And there was an array of stars. Did you record this? No we didn't record this. We gave a benefit performance. There were great benefits. You see in New York City they used to put my name on every program, whether I showed up or not, because I was a transferred member. I was only allowed to play in one place until six months had expired. You know the transfer member. And I played at the six day bicycle races with my band for the poor children's tours and I didn't ask the union and they find us ten dollars a piece. But everybody played for nothing but I said you should at least ask us could you play. I didn't think it was necessary. And when they announced my band you'd be surprised how many people from New Orleans were in this bicycle race, prize fighters, prize fighters, trainers, bums, and come up to see me. You know what I mean? And we played about four tunes and this is the truth. There were a lot of, Vincent Lopez, Paul Ash, all big shots sitting in a box, they'd offer a hundred dollars for a sprit to get the bicycle riders to race one another. Otherwise they'd just go around and around and say, Vincent Lopez offers a hundred dollars for a sprit. Vroom, they struck me. The next morning my phone ran incestually. Every agent wanted to book my band. And the only one I wanted to talk to was Vincent Lopez because I know him. You see? So I was under contract. The union allowed me to stay there for six months and then I'd have to join the union. And about that time I got enough of a union. I should have stayed there. I had everything in my home. I came home and people were glad to see me again. And I continued. But it's bad to play in one place too long. No matter how good you are they know what you're going to play before you play. They know how you play it, they can sing it. The only thing I loved about it was that I played, I had a job at Cowbs in the winter and I could go to the White House in the summer. They gave me a share of stock in the golf club. I didn't have to pay any green fees. I could go fishing. What did they set for? And I played three hours at night, no Sundays. Don't get it. Now, why don't you want to know?
